text: I’m reviewing the captured UDP run and the linked CLI parsing evidence. I’ll write only the new first-board review, preserving the existing reports and raw records.

The raw sender and receiver summaries agree on a completed 30-second UDP measurement, and the sender explicitly reports the final ACK. The pacing marker is absent, so this run contains no pacing-time measurement. Final snapshots show recovered IOB/page/address-space counts, but kernel heap use remains 11,936 bytes above baseline.

The source and linked binary both confirm the cause: `-b40M` parses to 41,943,040 bit/s, while the observation gate compares against 40,000,000. The nominal 1,470-byte spacing is therefore about 280.38 µs. I’ll record that correction and the limited recovery/cleanup evidence in the new review.

I’ll check the frozen read-probe code, linked fault branch, and ESP32-S31 register semantics to decide whether the SLV_END rejection is justified and what a bounded read-only follow-up could establish.

The trace identifies a deliberate fault-6 stop after the first USR operation completed; it does not identify a guard or status-read hang. The S31 headers define SLV_END as an FSM transition and separately define KEEP as forcing CS low. The current “SLV_END must stay clear under KEEP” assertion therefore needs a functional continuation test, rather than being treated as proof that the physical CS pin rose.

The archived flash ID matches XMC’s XM25UH128D family. Its manufacturer datasheet allows READ03h at up to 108 MHz at 2.7–3.6 V, or 80 MHz at 2.3–2.7 V, so a generic 50 MHz limit would be the wrong diagnosis. I’m checking the final event-clearing requirements for a four-segment read that records END events and still demands a fresh final completion, full data match, and safe restoration.

The SLV_END-with-KEEP rejection lacks sufficient justification as a physical CS failure criterion. Recommend one bounded, nonmutating four-segment READ that records events while retaining timeouts, strict command constraints, full comparison and restoration checks. This does not approve PP.

The matched XM25UH128D datasheet does not establish READ03 at 80 MHz as out of specification. Recovery records report full original-flash comparison completed at 12:36:30 UTC and UART released; no live verification performed.
